A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SerialGen and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Their corresponding methods and experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, architectural ablations, a 30-participant user study, and TikTok animation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds facial-similarity measurements, analysis of identity preservation at each stage, and an LCM-Lookahead comparison.

M1.justification: The two-stage pipeline, FBDM and RPIM components, personalization architecture, and training objectives remain unchanged. The new 'identity loss' analysis evaluates identity preservation rather than introducing an optimization loss.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic-character data, approximately 300,000-image personalization set, 40-character/20-prompt evaluation, and TikTok benchmark. Head-only inputs and nonhuman qualitative examples already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Supplementary Section 13 adds LCM-Lookahead as an evaluated comparator. IP-Adapter, FastComposer, StoryMaker, and the animation comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds ArcFace cosine similarity (Face Sim.) to the main and one-stage comparisons, and evaluates intermediate versus final outputs in Table 7. Existing splits, sample counts, training budgets, and user-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New supplementary Section 12 compares identity preservation after standardization and personalization. Figure 11 adds two head-only examples to the existing 3D-style-bias analysis. The earlier training-strategy, module, and token-count ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four randomized images per character–prompt combination. Neither adds seed information, repeated-training estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Previously reported scores are retained. New results include Face Sim. of 0.53 for SerialGen versus 0.54 for StoryMaker (Table 1); standardization versus personalization scores of 89.47/0.69 and 85.49/0.53 for CLIP-I/Face Sim. (Table 7); and LCM-Lookahead's 74.56 CLIP-I, 24.63 CLIP-T, and 0.46 Face Sim. (Section 13). Figure 11 also adds qualitative examples.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) and the mathematical model descriptions are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced; Face Sim. is an empirical evaluation addition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about standardization, text control, and appearance consistency. Replacing 'overall appearance' with 'whole-body appearance' preserves the scope already defined in v1.

C2.justification: v2 discusses StoryMaker's facial-similarity advantage and additional face encoder, and LCM-Lookahead's text-control versus consistency tradeoff. It also interprets identity retention after standardization and explains 3D-style clothing artifacts in head-only examples.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures in Section 4.1 and supplementary Section 6 retain the same hardware, training hyperparameters, data processing, sampling procedures, and RPIM details. The project link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on domain-agnostic tuning-encoders, apprenticeship learning, and LCM-Lookahead. The latter also extends the comparison with face-oriented personalization, while the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes 'whole-body' terminology, updates author and affiliation details, revises evaluation prose, and adds two short supplementary sections. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The comparison tables gain Face Sim. columns, Table 7 is added, and Figure 11 gains a third row. The user-study table moves from main-text Table 2 to supplementary Table 5; several figures are resized, relocated, or renumbered while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: Direct facial-similarity evaluation, the analysis of identity preservation at each stage, and the LCM-Lookahead comparison make the evidence more informative. Acknowledging StoryMaker's facial-similarity advantage and LCM-Lookahead's text-alignment advantage adds useful qualification. These are limited gains within unchanged methods and test coverage, without new uncertainty estimates.
